key_insight: InverFill replaces random noise initialization with a one-step inversion that yields an initial latent aligned to the visible background, enabling high-quality inpainting using only a few diffusion steps and avoiding harmonization artifacts.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between photorealistic diffusion inpainting and practical speed: it addresses semantic misalignment and visible artifacts that occur when few-step text-to-image diffusion samplers are naively applied to inpainting.
method: One-step inversion: compute an informed initial latent from the masked image so the inpainted region starts semantically aligned with the background instead of random Gaussian noise.
Integrate the inverted latent with a few-step diffusion sampler and the original conditioning (mask and context) to guide generation and preserve fidelity.
Design harmonization-aware sampling to reduce boundary artifacts and maintain consistent texture and semantics between the inpainted patch and surrounding image.
impact: Enables fast, practical image inpainting with diffusion models—delivering near-photoreal quality in far fewer sampling steps—making inpainting feasible for interactive editing, real-time applications, and resource-constrained deployments.
visual_elements: Before/after side-by-side examples showing naive few-step inpainting vs InverFill (highlighting reduced artifacts and better harmonization).
Pipeline diagram: masked image -> one-step inversion -> few-step diffusion sampler -> final inpainted image (with annotations).
Comparison chart: quality vs number of sampling steps for baseline vs InverFill (showing higher fidelity at low steps).
Close-up boundary zooms and semantic alignment heatmap to illustrate reduced mismatch at mask edges.
paper_title: InverFill: One-Step Inversion for Enhanced Few-Step Diffusion Inpainting
paper_authors: Duc Vu, Kien Nguyen, Trong-Tung Nguyen, Ngan Nguyen, Phong Nguyen
